references.text: Israel is warned against saying, 'My own power and the might of my hand have gained me this wealth,' reflecting God's concern that Israel would boast in their own strength.
Isaiah warns against boasting in one's own strength, just as God feared Israel would do after defeating Midian.
Paul explains that God chooses what is weak in the world so that no one may boast before Him, the same principle seen when God reduced Gideon's army.
The treasure in clay jars shows that the overwhelming power belongs to God and not to us, just as God used a small army to defeat Midian.
God's power is made perfect in weakness, the same principle God demonstrated by reducing Gideon's army.
The Lord can save by many or by few, showing that God's victory does not depend on the number of soldiers.
Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the Lord, shall victory be won—the same principle seen in Gideon's battle.
